what_happened: Companion .dotfiles task 'retire_machine_wide_sapience_surface' claims the seven sapience read-tool grants retract cleanly on unload and only the four write-tool grants are a known residual. Measured .claude-extensions.json shows the tracked array (permissions.children.allow.items) is empty for all eleven grants with no per-item provenance -- none would retract, not only the four. Report states the contradiction; correction must be carried across by hand since the other repo is out of this task's edit scope.

Dispatch scoped repair to sapience/nix/lean permissions.allow. Measurement found a fourth stale record not named in the dispatch: email's permissions.deny (7 items, tracked items: []), same dedup-before-track defect. Also found the defect class covers non-matcher hook-event arrays (sapience's SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/SessionEnd/Stop), not only permission arrays, contradicting the dispatch's blanket 'hooks escape this' framing for those four events specifically.

Plan phase re-validated the research report's scope-item-2 recommendation ([Regenerate]/manager.wipe repairs the stale tracking records) and found it incorrect: manager.regenerate calls settings_backup.restore BEFORE manager.resync_all, and settings_backup.BACKUP_FILES includes settings.local.json, so the wipe path restores the already-populated grant list as the merge base and the dedup-before-track defect fires again. The plan therefore selects a different repair route (plain redeploy AFTER the engine fix) and a different tracking shape than the report recommended.

merge_spec.lua is already 3-failed/21-passed headless before any change: read_host_fixture points at specs/369_orphan_sweep_for_removed_merge_target_entries/records/fixtures/host-settings.json, a task directory that no longer exists after archival/renumbering. The plan adds a first phase to recover the fixture from commit fc8cca3f0 and re-site it next to the spec, since the task's acceptance bar requires merge_spec to pass headless.
